The value each input starts at, and returns to

Source: R/calculator.R
mm_calculator_defaults.Rd

One definition read by the form and by the reset button, so that what "reset" restores cannot drift from what the form opened with.

Usage

mm_calculator_defaults(model)

Arguments

model

A mm_model().

Value

A named list, one element per predictor.

Details

Both come from the datadist's "Adjust to" row, which holds the median of each continuous predictor and the commonest level of each categorical one. That is the cohort's most ordinary member, and it is where the model is most certain, because the standard error of a prediction grows with distance from the middle of the data the model was fitted on. Opening there means the first number a reader sees is the one the model is best placed to make.

The obvious alternative, each factor's first level, is what this used to do, and it is worse in a way that is easy to miss: first levels are chosen for the model's arithmetic, not for how common they are, and combining one per predictor can produce somebody almost nobody is. On the ENT applicant model it opened on an international graduate needing work authorisation on a second attempt with no Step 2 score, whose interval was among the widest in the cohort.

A level the fit never saw cannot be offered, so an "Adjust to" value that is not in the schema falls back to the first level. That happens when a level was carried only by rows dropped for incompleteness.
